subject: Globex: EU list-price equalization & channel margin routing
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@globex.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@globex.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 16:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU list-price equalization request & channel margin routing

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups before we can take the Private Offer to legal:

1) Globex operates across multiple EU entities; external counsel flagged that AWS Marketplace list prices must be equalized across our EU accounts to avoid perceived transfer pricing issues. Can Redwood confirm you can offer the same list price across regions while allowing local channel margin pass-through?

2) On channel margin: we need the offer to show a 10% pass-through to our local reseller (they demand line-item visibility in the invoice). Is that supported in the Private Offer mechanics and invoice pathing? If not, what are the operational workarounds?

3) Any constraints on committing to a 12-month reserved capacity SKU vs. a metered bundle for the EU region? Procurement prefers predictable monthly invoicing.

Attached: high-level SOW and our standard procurement questionnaire (only the SOW reference here).

Can you propose next steps and any documentation we should include for our internal audit?

Thanks,
Raj
Procurement Manager, Globex Corporation

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@globex.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2025 17:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU list-price equalization request & channel margin routing

Hi Raj — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and a suggested path forward: 

- List-price equalization: yes, we can present the same list price across defined EU tenant identifiers in the Private Offer. The caveat is that committed-reserved SKUs and metered SKUs are managed differently in the marketplace catalog, so we’d map the committed SKU to an equivalence group for reporting. That will show the same list price; discounts / private-offer netting can be applied per account.

- Channel margin pass-through: we support invoice-level line items that reflect channel pass-through. For AWS specifically we typically route a reseller uplift via a separate invoice line (invoice routing + partner settlement). If Globex needs direct visibility on the Marketplace invoice, we can do a reseller pass-through that shows 10% as a separate line and provide an accompanying CSV for settlement reconciliation. I attached a short spreadsheet with two routing patterns (direct pass-through vs. reseller-settlement).

- Billing preference: for predictable monthly invoicing the committed 12-month reserved capacity SKU is the cleanest — it reduces per-token variance and gives you consistent invoice lines. Metered bundles can be billed monthly but have usage variance. If procurement wants a hybrid, we can do a committed baseline + overage metered SKU.

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ll schedule a 30-min call to align on which catalog SKU mapping you prefer (committed vs hybrid).
2) We’ll produce an evidentiary packet for your audit: marketplace listing equivalence documentation, invoice sample showing reseller pass-through, and our channel settlement playbook.
3) If Globex confirms the 10% reseller line and baseline SKU, we’ll prepare a draft Private Offer + DocuSign.

Attaching: proposal_v1_Globex.pdf and channel_margin_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet shows both routing patterns and sample invoice rows).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Marketplace Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@globex.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:03:00 +0100
Subject: Fwd: Re: EU list-price equalization request & channel margin routing

Hi Raj — forwarding a short note from our channel ops and finance lead (Marcus) below. We can do the 10% pass-through as a visible invoice line; the reconciliation flow we typically use is:

- Private Offer list price is equalized across EU entities in the catalog; net price per-entity is controlled by the private-offer discount.
- We emit a separate reseller Uplift line on the invoice (10% of the line item). That line is flagged in the invoice metadata for your accounting team so you can route settlement to the local reseller.
- For audit purposes we will provide a monthly settlement CSV and a two-month lookback ledger for the first 6 months.

Marcus, can you confirm the DocuSign and invoice sample timeline for Globex?

Cheers,
Jordan
Senior Deals Ops — Redwood Inference

* DocuSign timeline: once Globex signs the SOW + Private Offer, we can turn on the invoice routing within 3 business days; first reconciled CSV delivered with the following billing cycle.
